Content: The Tepper School of Business Undergraduate Student Handbook provides policies, expectations, and resources to support the Tepper School experience. It is intended for all Tepper students, faculty, and staff. Policies are subject to annual revision, and URLs are current as of August 2024. No part may be reproduced without written permission from the Tepper School. For questions, contact Jennifer Wegner, Ed.D., Assistant Dean, Undergraduate Programs (jwegner@andrew.cmu.edu).

Each member of the Carnegie Mellon community must be familiar with relevant university policies. This handbook reproduces sections from The Word: Student Handbook and the Undergraduate Catalog; direct questions to the Undergraduate Programs Office.

Tepper School Community Expectations: Tepper fosters a diverse, inclusive environment based on trust, respect, and support. Every community member must contribute daily to this culture of excellence.

Tepper School Undergraduate Programs Office: Located in the Tepper Building, suite 2400, Monday–Friday 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m., it administers program logistics, academic advising, support for student clubs, professional trips, community programs, and New Student Orientation.

All Carnegie Mellon community members must uphold CMU’s policies. This section reproduces excerpts from The Word: Student Handbook and the Undergraduate Catalog. It is each student’s responsibility to know and follow academic, conduct, and safety policies. Violations carry serious consequences, up to dismissal.

CMU students must maintain the highest standards of personal, ethical, and moral conduct. Academic work must be original, properly credited, and honest. Any violation of integrity undermines the community’s trust and the value of CMU degrees. Students unable to uphold these principles should voluntarily withdraw.

Carnegie Mellon University does not discriminate in admission, employment, or program access based on race, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, creed, ancestry, belief, veteran status, or genetic information. Inquiries regarding compliance should be directed to the University Ombudsman (5000 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15213; 412-268-1018).

Students are encouraged to maintain proper nutrition, regular exercise, adequate sleep, and effective stress management. Counseling and Psychological Services (CaPS) is available for academic stress, life events, anxiety, or depression; early intervention is advised. For immediate concerns, contact CaPS via the UHS portal or visit their office.

The Tepper School community values diversity, inclusion, and mutual respect. Students, faculty, and staff must contribute to a supportive environment by demonstrating professionalism, integrity, and collaboration in all interactions.

Located in the Tepper Building, suite 2400, this office operates Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m. It oversees undergraduate program administration, academic advising, student club support, professional treks, community outreach, and New Student Orientation activities.

The Tepper School offers Bachelor of Science degrees in Business Administration and Economics, plus minors, additional majors, and accelerated pathways. Each program is governed by the Undergraduate Catalog corresponding to the student’s entry year. Advisors guide students through program requirements, policy interpretation, and resource navigation.

Each Tepper student is assigned an academic advisor who provides guidance on course selection, concentration/minor declaration, study abroad planning, transfer credits, and policy questions. Economics and Business Administration students follow a two-stage advising model: first‐year advising via Dietrich (Economics) or Tepper (Business), then a departmental advisor upon declaration. Tepper adheres to CMU’s Statement on Advising.

Advising appointments are scheduled via ScheduleOnce. Students must attend or cancel via the same system if unable to make an appointment due to illness or conflict. Advisors expect timely attendance and preparation for each meeting.

Stellic is CMU’s degree‐audit and planning platform. It displays a student’s progress, highlights double‐count risks, and allows exceptions (once approved by the advisor). Stellic is unofficial; the academic transcript is official. Students are responsible for monitoring their audit and should consult their advisor if discrepancies arise.

Tepper and CMU expect original work on every graded assignment. Unauthorized collaboration or use of external assistance is prohibited unless explicitly allowed by the instructor. Students may seek help from the Student Academic Success Center (SASC) or Academic Resource Center (ARC) if permitted. Academic integrity violations are handled by the Office of Community Responsibility (OCR). Students cannot drop a course under active integrity investigation until the matter is resolved.

Students should regularly review their academic records via Stellic and SIO (Student Information Online). Advisors also review records during advising. If coursework or grades are missing, students must notify their advisor immediately to initiate resolution.

CMU awards course equivalency credit for qualifying scores on AP, IB, and Cambridge A‐Levels. There is no maximum AP credit cap at CMU. AP credits do not factor into QPA but count toward degree units. If a student subsequently enrolls in the CMU course for which AP credit was granted, the AP credit is removed and replaced by the new grade. Students cannot receive credit for both AP and the equivalent CMU course.

Academic standing is determined each semester based on semester QPA, cumulative QPA, and progress toward degree (completion of at least 80% of attempted units; grades N, W, and R do not count as completed units).

• Good Standing (Departmental): Semester and cumulative QPA ≥ 2.0, and completion of ≥ 80% of attempted units.  
• Academic Concern (Departmental): Semester QPA < 2.0 or < 80% completion. Students receive an Academic Concern letter and must meet with their advisor to create an Academic Success Plan. Reviewed each semester; return to Good Standing by achieving ≥ 2.0 QPA and ≥ 36 completed units.  
• Academic Warning (Departmental): Semester QPA < 2.0 and/or < 36 completed units or cumulative QPA < 2.0. Students on warning must create an Academic Success Plan, cannot overload, and must meet warning conditions (≥ 2.0 QPA, ≥ 36 units, cumulative ≥ 2.0) to return to Good Standing.  
• Academic Suspension (University): Failure to meet warning requirements may result in a one‐year suspension. Suspended students work with their advisor and the Assistant Dean on a return plan. To return, submit required materials by the deadline.  
• Final Warning (Departmental): After suspension, returning students are on final warning with specific conditions. Failure to meet final warning conditions results in Academic Drop (expulsion).  
• Drop (University): Permanent expulsion from Tepper, typically following failure to meet final warning conditions.

Undergraduate students may audit courses per the Undergraduate Catalog. Audited courses do not earn credit or factor into QPA. Students must register to audit before the drop deadline and obtain instructor and advisor approval. Each department may impose additional audit requirements.

Students may drop a course before or on the drop deadline as published in the Academic Calendar. Dropped courses are removed from the schedule and transcript. If dropping below 36 units (full‐time), advisor and college approval are required; international students must consult OIE to maintain visa status.  

Late Drop Vouchers: Each undergraduate receives three vouchers to drop or elect Pass/No‐Pass (P/N) after the deadline, one voucher per semester. The advisor initiates the voucher request in SIO; the student has 24 hours to confirm the drop. Vouchers are not intended for exceptional circumstances (e.g., health crises are exempt under separate processes).

To appeal a course grade, follow the process outlined in The Word: Student Handbook. Appeals are handled by the Office of Community Responsibility (OCR). Advisors are not involved in the grade appeal process.

Required degree courses must be graded with a letter grade (A–D). Pass/No‐Pass (P/N) is allowed only for specific courses (e.g., Core@CM, First‐Year Writing) or during approved circumstances (e.g., Spring 2020 P/N election). Repeating a course does not remove the original grade; both grades appear on the transcript and both factor into QPA. P grades count toward total units but do not factor into QPA; N grades earn no credit and do not lower QPA. Departmental grading policies may vary; students should consult the syllabus and advisor.

Full‐time status requires a minimum of 36 units per semester. To graduate in eight semesters, students typically take about 45 units each term. Dropping below 36 units requires advisor and college approval. International students must consult with the Office of International Education (OIE) before dropping below full‐time to maintain visa compliance.

Students register for courses via Student Information Online (SIO). Registration times are assigned by class level and rotate each term. Advisors expect students to consult before registration and use SIO for planning. If schedule conflicts arise, students should work with their advisor to identify alternatives. Late adds require instructor and advisor approval before the add deadline.

When courses are full, students may join waitlists. Priority is assigned in the following order: (1) primary Tepper majors (Business Administration/Economics), (2) Tepper additional majors/minors, (3) non‐Tepper students. Waitlist placement is determined by major, class level, position on the list, and seat availability. Each department manages its own waitlist per Registrar policy. To remain on a waitlist, students must respond to “tag up” prompts when notified. There is no guarantee of enrollment; students should have backup plans.

After the drop deadline and before the tenth week of classes, students may withdraw from a course, which results in a W grade on the transcript. W grades count as attempted units but do not factor into QPA. To withdraw, students submit a withdrawal form with advisor approval. Withdrawals after the tenth week require exceptional vouchers or petitions. Students with active academic integrity investigations may have special withdrawal procedures.

Tepper undergraduates may cross‐register for approved courses at participating University of Pittsburgh and affiliated institutions through the PCHE program. Eligibility requires good academic standing and completion of prerequisites. Students must obtain approval from both their Tepper advisor and the host institution’s registrar. Cross‐registration forms are submitted via Scotty. Transferred credits apply per equivalency guidelines; consult the Registrar for details.

Tepper’s degree requirements, including core courses, concentrations, and general education, are defined in the Undergraduate Catalog corresponding to the student’s entry year. Internal transfers should confirm exact requirements with their advisor to ensure timely progress toward graduation.

Tepper students who earn a semester QPA of 3.75 or higher, complete at least 36 factorable units, and have no incomplete grades in fall or spring are named to the Dean’s List. Qualifying names are published on the Tepper website at the end of each semester.

To pursue a dual degree, students must complete at least 90 additional units beyond their primary degree requirements, including general education and concentration requirements for both degrees. Applicants submit dual degree petitions via their advisor and must obtain approval from both departments. The dual degree fulfills the minor requirement of the primary major when completed concurrently. Graduates receive two diplomas and may participate in the Tepper diploma ceremony.

Students entering Fall 2020 or later follow the University Core requirements, while those who matriculated before Fall 2020 follow the Breadth requirements. Core or Breadth courses may double‐count toward general education and minors/additional majors, subject to departmental constraints. Consult the Undergraduate Catalog for detailed course lists.

Tepper offers accelerated master’s pathways (3-1-1 programs) that allow undergraduates to earn bachelor’s and master’s degrees in five years. Eligible programs, application deadlines, and prerequisites are detailed in the Course Catalog. Interested students should discuss options with their advisor and the Graduate Admissions Office early in their junior year.

To graduate, students must complete all program requirements per the Undergraduate Catalog of their entry year, maintain a cumulative QPA of at least 2.0, and satisfy residence and financial obligations. Students with 36 or fewer remaining units may participate in the diploma ceremony but receive diplomas only after completing all requirements. “Factorable units” count toward QPA; “passed units” count toward the 364-unit degree requirement.

Subheading: Honors Thesis for Primary and Additional Majors
Content: Students may qualify for College Honors by completing an 18-unit, two‐semester senior research thesis (ENGMGT 70304 and 70305) under faculty supervision. The thesis culminates in a written report and a public presentation at Meeting of the Minds. Eligibility requires completion of at least 75% of undergraduate units (approximately 273 units) and departmental approval. Non-Tepper additional majors may apply for Tepper College Honors by petitioning the Honors Committee.

An Incomplete (I) grade may be granted when a student has completed at least 75% of coursework but cannot finish due to extenuating circumstances. The instructor and student agree in writing on the remaining work and timeline. If the Incomplete is not resolved by the deadline, a default grade (typically F) is assigned and factored into QPA. See the Undergraduate Catalog for full policy details.

Independent Study allows qualified undergraduates to pursue specialized topics under faculty supervision for 3–9 units. Eligibility requires good academic standing and identification of a CMU faculty sponsor in the relevant discipline. The project must be directly related to the student’s major or minor. Submit the Independent Study application, signed by the faculty sponsor, to the Undergraduate Programs Office by the add deadline. Only one Independent Study may satisfy a degree requirement, and it cannot substitute for an existing catalog course.

Tepper students may earn academic credit for business-related internships via courses 70-499 or 73-111 (3 units, P/N grading). Eligibility: must be a Tepper major/minor in good standing, possess an internship offer letter, and submit a one-paragraph description of duties and learning objectives. International students requiring Curricular Practical Training (CPT) must submit the internship application, offer letter, and description to the Undergraduate Programs Office by the add deadline. Non-Tepper students must complete at least 60% of additional major coursework prior to the internship and 70% by semester’s end. All internship arrangements require advisor approval and Registrar pre-approval.

Students may request a Leave of Absence (LOA) in consultation with their advisor for medical, personal, or academic reasons. W grades are assigned for courses in progress based on timing and circumstances. During LOA, students remain in good standing and have remote program support. To return, students complete LOA reentry paperwork, obtain signatures from their advisor and the Assistant Dean, and submit the form by the reentry deadline.

Subheading: Major Change within the Tepper School
Content:
Students may change majors within the Tepper School by meeting departmental criteria and submitting the Change of Major form via Scotty.  

• Economics + Mathematics: Declared B.S. Economics students with cumulative QPA ≥ 3.5; completion of 73-102, 21-127/21-128, 21-241, 73-103, and 73-230/73-240 with grades B or higher; submit the B.S. in Computational and Financial Mathematics (BSCF) application via Dietrich College.  
• Computational Finance: Complete BSCF prerequisites through Mathematical Sciences—courses 21-127/21-128, 21-241/21-242, and 21-270.  
• Switching Tepper Majors: Must complete at least one full semester in the current major before requesting a change (e.g., Business Administration to Economics after Fall semester). Consult advisors in both departments for planning.

Pass/No-Pass (P/N): Students may elect P/N grading by the published deadline each semester. A “P” counts toward total degree units but generally does not apply to major or minor requirements unless explicitly permitted (e.g., Core@CM, First-Year Writing). P grades do not factor into QPA; N grades yield no credit and do not lower QPA. P/N elections after the drop deadline require a voucher. Some courses (e.g., Tepper core courses or departmental requirements) prohibit P/N without explicit permission.

Students may request exemptions from Tepper or CMU policy by submitting a Policy Exemption Request Form via their academic advisor. The request must include a clear rationale, supporting documentation, and specify which policy section is requested for an exception. The Assistant Dean reviews all requests and provides written decisions. Common exemptions include overload petitions, minor substitutions, or late Add/Drop petitions.

Students are expected to read Tepper communications regularly. The weekly Tepper Undergraduate newsletter includes academic updates, club events, career opportunities, and deadlines. Important announcements (e.g., registration, scholarship deadlines, curriculum changes) are sent via email to the student’s CMU address. Tepper also maintains a dedicated Canvas site where course resources, academic updates, and event postings are shared. Students are auto-enrolled and should check Canvas daily.

The Student Defined Major (SDM) allows motivated students to propose a custom interdisciplinary major not otherwise offered. To apply, students meet with the Assistant Dean to discuss concept, coursework, and learning objectives. SDM proposals require approval from two or more CMU faculty sponsors, the Assistant Dean, and the Registrar. Students must be in good academic standing to submit an SDM application. Once approved, SDM students work with an advisor team and must meet SDM milestones to remain in the program.

Tepper students may participate in exchange or affiliate programs through the Office of International Education (OIE). Eligibility: cumulative QPA ≥ 2.0 (some programs require higher QPA). Applications open at least one year before departure. Students submit a Study Abroad Transfer Credit (SATC) form listing planned courses and have equivalencies evaluated. Approved courses transfer as specified; students must update the SATC if course plans change. Financial aid and scholarships may apply; consult Financial Aid prior to departure.

Tepper-affiliated student organizations have priority for reserving space in the Tepper Building. Reservation requests are submitted through the Tepper Undergraduate Programs Office at least two weeks in advance. Requests must include event details, expected attendance, and AV needs. Priority is given to academic or recognized student groups. Cancellations require 48 hours’ notice to avoid penalties. Non-Tepper groups may request space campus-wide via 25Live.

Tepper seniors with a cumulative QPA ≥ 3.5 may petition to enroll in select Tepper graduate courses. Enrollment is not guaranteed; space is limited, and MBA core courses are often restricted. Interested students must petition through their academic advisor and obtain departmental approval. Graduate course credit may apply toward elective requirements but cannot replace required undergraduate coursework.

Tepper offers minors in:  
• Business Administration  
• Business Analytics & Optimization  
• Economics  
• Financial Management  
• Operations & Supply Chain Management  
• Product Management  
• Innovation & Entrepreneurship (IDeATE)  

Eligibility and requirements:  
• Meet prerequisite courses with a minimum grade (typically C or better).  
• Adhere to primary major grading policies (minimum QPA, letter grades, repeat rules).  
• Economics minor requiring 73-102 may be waived; if waived, students substitute nine elective units (course numbers 70xxx or 73xxx) to meet the 54-unit minor requirement.  
• Upon completion, minors are certified by the Tepper Undergraduate Programs Office and recorded on transcripts (minors do not appear on diplomas).

Students graduating with a final cumulative QPA ≥ 3.50 earn University Honors and are recognized at Commencement. Honors designation is noted on the transcript. No separate application is required; eligibility is determined at graduation.

Additional Major in Business Administration: Applicants must complete a Tepper Business Administration minor, course 70-207 (Probability & Statistics for Business) or equivalent, and course 21-120 (Differential & Integral Calculus) with minimum grade C. Additional major students follow primary major grading and academic policies. Upon completion, the additional major is certified and appears on the diploma.  

Concentration Requirement (Primary Majors): Business Administration majors must complete one concentration and the required number of business elective units per catalog. Students must select a concentration in Stellic by the end of their sophomore year. Concentration and business electives may not double-count against other BA requirements, including the minor.  

Additional Major Holders: Students with a Business Administration additional major have the minor and concentration requirements waived; they must complete at least 27 units of business elective courses.  

Product Management Majors: Product Management majors who also have an HCII minor or additional major have HCII course requirements waived; they must complete one additional Tepper elective in Product Management.  

Course Double Counts: No double counting is allowed between concentration/elective requirements and other Business Administration requirements. Double counts with other departments (e.g., minors, additional majors, dual degrees) follow that department’s policy. No double counts between minors and home-college general education. Non-Tepper minors/additional majors follow their home college’s catalog rules. If a student pursues multiple Tepper minors, only one course may double count across minors.  

Minor & Additional Major Options: Business Administration majors must complete a minor; some fulfill this with an additional major. Each college manages its own declaration process. Upon declaration, students meet regularly with both their minor/additional major advisor and Tepper advisor. Completion of an additional major waives the minor and concentration requirements but requires at least 27 units of business electives. The minor or additional major must be certified by the relevant department at graduation; failure to complete certification prevents graduation.  

Pass Grades: A maximum of nine “P” units may count toward the 364-unit BA requirement (excluding Core@CM). Spring 2020 P/N exceptions apply per university policy.  

Semester Course Overload: In fall or spring, a normal load is five full-semester courses (approximately 45 units); overloading occurs when students register for more than 51 units (up to 57 units with a petition). Eligibility requires cumulative QPA ≥ 3.5. New first-year students and external transfers are limited to 50 units in their first semester and cannot overload until completing one semester. Overload petitions are reviewed by the Tepper Undergraduate Programs Office; students whose cumulative QPA falls below 3.5 after overloading may lose overload eligibility.  

Transfer Credit: Tepper awards transfer credit for courses meeting CMU’s academic rigor as determined by Tepper faculty. Students must earn at least a C− unless departmental policy specifies otherwise. Exemptions include Washington Semester, CMU-Q courses, and accredited community college or approved online courses as per department policy. BA Dual Degree students follow Tepper transfer policy.  
• Required Tepper courses must be taken at CMU: Business Science (70106), Business Leadership Endeavor (70104, 70204, 70304), Senior Capstone Management Game (70401) or approved equivalent, First-Year Writing (76101, 76102/76106, 76107/76108), and Core@CM (99101).  
• BA students may transfer up to 90 units total (including study abroad) to degree requirements: maximum of five courses from U.S. institutions; maximum of two toward business foundation; maximum of one toward concentration/electives; maximum of one toward business core; maximum of three toward general education.  
• Dual enrollment high school courses require a college transcript and instructor credentials; evaluated per CMU equivalency procedures.  
• External transfers admitted to Tepper may transfer up to 182 units (including AP/IB and CMU-Q credits); no additional transfer credit is permitted outside of study abroad exceptions.  
• Non-Tepper students pursuing a Tepper minor/additional major may transfer up to nine units toward the minor and up to 27 units toward the additional major. Consult the Tepper Undergraduate Programs Office for specific equivalencies.
Tags: BA policies, additional major, concentration, overload, transfer

Content:
Additional Major & Minor: CMU undergraduates may pursue Economics as an additional major or minor. Students must meet with Tepper to review requirements and submit the additional major application after completing minor prerequisites.  

Course Double Counts:  
• BA in Economics: No double counts across degree requirements.  
• BS in Economics: No double counts across degree requirements.  
• BS in Economics & Mathematics: Three economics electives and three math electives must be unique (no double counts).  
• Economics Additional Major: Four advanced economics electives must be unique and cannot double count with any other major or minor.  
• Economics Minor: Course 73-265 and three economics electives must be unique and not double count with other requirements.  

Economics & Mathematical Sciences Program: Prepares students for Ph.D. programs in economics, mathematics, or business research. Admission criteria: cumulative QPA ≥ 3.5; completion of 73-102; grade B or higher in one of 21-127/21-128; grade B or higher in 21-241; grade B or higher in 73-103; grade B or higher in one of 73-230/73-240.  

First-Year Advising: First-year Economics prospects begin with a Dietrich Success Center (DSC) advisor. Prospective Economics majors are encouraged to meet with the Tepper Economics advisor for resources and community support.  

Graduate School Preparation: Doctoral programs value analytical skills, research experience, GRE scores, and faculty recommendations. Students aiming for Ph.D. pathways should discuss plans with advisors and consider the B.S. in Economics & Mathematical Sciences.  

Minor Requirement for BA/BS Economics Students & Additional Major Option: Students entering Fall 2023 or later require a minor for BA/BS Economics; some fulfill this with an additional major. Each college manages its own declaration process. Students should meet regularly with minor/additional major advisors and Tepper advisors. An additional major waives the minor requirement; certification by the corresponding department is required at graduation.  

Omicron Delta Epsilon Honor Society: Induction requirements include pursuing Economics (primary, additional major, or minor), completion of 73-102 or 73-104, 73-230, 73-240, and at least one advanced elective; 36 units of economics at CMU Pittsburgh (excluding 73-101, 73-155, 73-450); cumulative QPA ≥ 3.0; economics QPA ≥ 3.0; junior or senior standing.  

Senior Experience: Fulfills degree requirements via 73-497 (Senior Seminar) or an Honors Thesis. 73-497 counts as an upper-level elective for BA, BS Economics, BS Economics & Mathematics, or BS Economics & Politics, but not for BS Economics & Statistics.  

Transfer Credit: Transfer courses are evaluated by Tepper’s equivalency process.  
• BA Economics: Maximum of 18 units of economics electives.  
• BS Economics: Maximum of 18 units of economics electives.  
• BS Economics & Mathematics: Maximum of nine units of economics electives.  
• Economics Additional Major: Maximum of 18 units of economics.  
• Economics Minor: Maximum of 18 units of economics electives.  
Consult Tepper for specific equivalencies.
Tags: economics, additional major, minor, double counts, transfer

Content: The CPDC helps students optimize their professional potential through career exploration, experiential learning, and employer connections. Services include individual career consultations, resume and interview preparation, and access to Handshake for internships, jobs, and campus positions. CPDC also coordinates career fairs and employer networking events.

Subheading: Center for Student Diversity and Inclusion
Content: An interdivisional center providing resources and programming for historically underrepresented and first-generation students. Located in the Cohon Center (lower level), it fosters access, inclusion, and intergroup dialogue. Services include mentoring programs, identity-based student organizations support, and diversity education workshops.

Computing Services offers IT resources for students, including file storage and sharing, email protection, network support, and account management. Services include OIT Help Desk support, CMU wireless network access, license management for campus-wide software, and security training modules.

CaPS provides confidential mental health support, including short-term psychotherapy, crisis intervention, and referrals to community resources. Initial consultations clarify therapeutic options. CaPS offers individual counseling (6–8 sessions on average at no cost), group therapy, psychiatry referrals, and campus outreach programs for stress management and resilience.

The HUB delivers comprehensive administrative support, including financial aid counseling, billing inquiries, payment processing, registration assistance, transcript requests, and academic records management. HUB advisors help students navigate university processes such as course enrollment, financial obligations, and scholarship applications.

OCR advises on community standards and complex student conduct issues. It serves as a resource for students, families, and faculty regarding academic integrity, behavioral concerns, and resolution processes. OCR coordinates educational sanctions, conducts hearings, and promotes ethical conduct across campus.

ODR supports students with physical, sensory, or learning disabilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. Students self-disclose disabilities prior to arrival to develop an Accommodation Plan. ODR issues Accommodation Memoranda for advisors and instructors and coordinates exam accommodations, assistive technology, and classroom accessibility.

OIE promotes and manages study abroad and exchange opportunities, supports international students with immigration compliance, and liaises with global academic partners. Services include visa advising, pre-departure orientation, cross-cultural programming, and on-site support for students abroad.

Subheading: Office of Undergraduate Research and Scholar Development
Content: This office provides seed funding, recognition, and conference travel support for undergraduate research. It administers grant opportunities, organizes workshops on research methods, and hosts Meeting of the Minds, CMU’s annual undergraduate research symposium. Students receive guidance on research proposals, conference abstracts, and publication opportunities.
Tags: undergraduate research, funding, Meeting of the Minds

Content: This office supports students’ spiritual and religious practices, offering cross-tradition programs to foster interfaith understanding. Services include Chaplaincy support, student-led religious organizations, prayer and meditation space bookings, and events promoting religious diversity and dialogue.

SASC offers academic support services—group workshops and individual tutoring—to develop study skills, time management, test preparation, and critical reading strategies. SASC helps students build confident, independent learning habits through one-on-one consultations and peer mentoring programs.

Subheading: Student Leadership, Involvement, and Civic Engagement (SLICE)
Content: SLICE provides opportunities for undergraduate leadership development, involvement, and civic engagement aligned with students’ interests and talents. Services include leadership workshops, student organization advising, community service partnerships, and co-curricular event planning support.

UHS provides general medical care to enrolled students, staffed by physicians, advanced practice clinicians, and nurses. Nurse visits are free; physician visits incur a small fee; prescriptions, laboratory tests, and specialist referrals are at student expense. UHS administers the Student Health Insurance Program, covering most Student Health Services fees. UHS also offers nutrition counseling, substance use support, and wellness education.

University Libraries offer academic support, research consultation, and access to a broad range of resources. Services include market research databases, investment data, company profiles, business news, and interlibrary loan. Online resources include e-books, journals, films, and specialized business and economics databases. Librarians provide workshops on research methods, citation management, and data analysis tools.
